story_type: ground-based interceptor fired from a silo at a ballistic missile target
hook: Fired out of an underground silo to hit a missile in space.
narration: This missile was fired out of an underground silo to hit another missile in space.
First, a cargo jet dropped the target over the Pacific near Hawaii, and its motor lit.
Then the interceptor launched from Vandenberg in California.
It carries no warhead. Its kill vehicle destroys the target by ramming it at enormous speed.
[short pause] This time its third stage was told not to fire, so the kill vehicle let go early.
outcome: The upgraded interceptor hit the target missile, a successful intercept.
title: Missile fired from a silo hits a missile
description:
The Missile Defense Agency's FTG-12 test: an upgraded Ground-Based Interceptor launched from Vandenberg Space Force Base intercepts an air-launched intermediate range ballistic missile target, Dec. 11, 2023.

question_comment: Could you hit a bullet with a bullet? Would you trust this system?

facts.claim: Successful intercept of an IRBM by an upgraded GBI
facts.source_quote: conducted a successful intercept today of an Intermediate Range Ballistic Missile (IRBM) by an upgraded Ground-Based Interceptor (GBI).

facts.claim: Third stage commanded not to ignite, earlier release of the kill vehicle
facts.source_quote: This test was also the first test of a three-stage GBI operating in two-stage mode, which means the third stage was commanded not to ignite and allowed earlier release of the kill vehicle, providing closer range engagements.
The test employed an upgraded GBI with a Capability Enhanced-II Block 1 Exo-Atmospheric Kill Vehicle.
